scope: Current process architecture and a separate, undeployed target design

current_implementation.claim: The shell launcher selects either harness or WAF execution; WAF never goes through harness Broker.
Broker, application translation, fixture adapter, scoring and evidence logging are functions in the harness process.
assist calls a local planning endpoint through Broker and only saves selected catalog IDs for review.
The native application adapter attaches private synthetic sessions and translates catalog requests.
run_pilot starts the application server as a subprocess, calls harness in-process, and later reads state and audit files.
The target application directly calls its configured local model; there is no management model broker on this path.
Retrieval is simple SQLite-backed synthetic tenant retrieval, not a deployed vector database or external RAG service.
WAF Python validates exact target and scope then starts bounded curl subprocesses and writes consolidated evidence.

claims: Trusted controller, model access broker, typed tool broker and independent isolation are proposed.
Inference endpoints aggregate local service and approved frontier APIs; provider access is routed by the model broker.
PyRIT target requests must use approved brokered adapters.
Installed tools are inventory, not executed campaign components.
OpenClaw, signed approvals, VM/network containment and protected evidence collection are not implemented in the local harness.

corrections: Separated process architecture from workflow functions.
Added the distinct planner and target-inference paths.
Connected WAF execution within its own view.
Removed the implication of a standalone authenticated approval or independently protected evidence service.
Separated the proposed lab from current implementation.
known_limits: This is an architectural summary; arrows show primary dependencies rather than every read/write.
Human independent review and actual-model calibration remain pending.
